intro.body: Flying Fridge is your family's shared noticeboard: one place for the everyday things that are easy to forget. Here's what each part does and how to use it — pick a section below.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.summary: One glance at the whole board — a count per module, a recent-items list, and a month calendar.
steps: The cards at the top summarise each module (open tasks, notices on the board, and so on) — select one to jump straight in.
Below the cards, switch between Recent and Calendar by tapping the tabs.
Recent lists everything happening within a couple of days of the chosen date, colour-coded by type; undated things sit at the bottom.
Calendar shows this month with a coloured dot per type on each day — tap a day to see it in Recent, and use 'Back to today' to return.
dashboard.tip: Dates come from each item itself — a task's due date, a notice's date, or when a pantry item stops being fresh.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.summary: Chores and to-dos for the family, colour-coded by their target date so what's urgent stands out.
steps: Open Tasks and add one with a short description.
Optionally set a target date — the dashboard colour-codes tasks by how close that date is.
Assign a task to yourself so nobody else picks it up; your assigned tasks gather in their own section.
Mark it done when finished — it stays in the timeline even after it leaves the board.
tasks.tip: No target date? The task still lives on the board — dates just drive the colour coding and calendar.

notices.title: Notices & Info
notices.summary: Simple announcements that stay on the board for a month, or longer if you make them permanent.
steps: Post a notice with the info the family should see.
Add an optional date if the notice is about a specific day.
It stays on the noticeboard for one month, or until someone takes it down.
Mark it permanent to keep it up until it's pulled down.
Mark it important to give it a colour highlight so it stands out.
notices.tip: Use 'important' for things people must not miss, and 'permanent' for standing info like the Wi-Fi password.

lostFound.title: Lost & Found
lostFound.summary: Post something you're looking for; it stays up, with its posting date, until it's found or you take it down.
steps: Add what you're looking for with a short description (a photo helps).
The posting date is shown so everyone sees how long it's been missing.
Family members can help locate it.
Take it down once it's found — it stays in the timeline either way.
lostFound.tip: Old, unresolved posts are easy to spot by their posting date.

pantry.title: Pantry
pantry.summary: Track food at home — when it was made, how long it stays good, and roughly how much is left.
steps: Add a food item with when it was made and how long it's likely to stay good.
Set an approximate quantity so everyone understands how much there is.
Anyone can increase or reduce the amount as it's used.
Mark it consumed to remove it from the list — it's kept in the timeline.
pantry.tip: Freshness comes from when it was made plus how long it keeps — check before you cook.

questions.title: Questions
questions.summary: Ask the family anything that needs a group answer or a quick decision.
steps: Post a question — for example, 'Pizza or pasta on Friday?'.
Family members chime in with answers.
Keep the discussion in one place instead of scattered messages.
Close it once it's answered; it stays in the timeline for later.
questions.tip: Great for quick decisions without a dozen back-and-forth texts.

appearance.title: Appearance & accessibility
appearance.summary: Make Flying Fridge comfortable — colour themes, light/dark, and full keyboard access.
steps: Use the colour-theme picker in the top bar to switch palettes (Blueberry, Grape, Forest, Ocean).
Choose High Contrast for maximum legibility.
Use the sun/moon button to switch light and dark — by default it follows your device.
Everything is keyboard-navigable: press Tab to move, and use the skip link to jump to the content.
appearance.tip: Prefer less motion? Flying Fridge respects your system's reduced-motion setting automatically.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.summary: A live feed of what the family adds to the board, with an unread badge on the bell and optional device alerts.
steps: When anyone adds a task, notice, lost & found post, pantry item, or question, everyone else is notified.
The bell in the top bar shows how many are unread — open it to see the feed.
Select a notification to jump straight to that section of the board.
Turn on device alerts to get a system notification when the app is open but in the background.
notifications.tip: Alerts while the app is fully closed need push (FCM), which is on the roadmap — the in-app feed and badge work today.
